title: RunState
description: Written to run-state.json; the top-level state of a review run.

status.description: `planned` is a DRY RUN: the plan, panel and preflight resolved and the run stopped before its first model call. Such a run has no findings because it looked at nothing — never because the tree was clean.

authority.description: The INCLUSION MANIFEST of the authority/context documents this run was judged against — the same entries written to authority/inclusion-manifest.json (see authority-manifest.schema.json). ABSENT when the run declared no authority, so a run that uses none is byte-identical to one written before the feature existed.

withheld.description: Files a CONTAINMENT rule kept out of the reviewed set (today: hardlinked regular files, which are withheld rather than halting the run). ABSENT when nothing was withheld, so a run that withheld nothing is byte-identical to one written before the feature existed. An entry is a gap in coverage: a reviewer cannot object to a file it was never shown.

trace.description: The caller's W3C trace context, CARRIED VERBATIM from the request that started this run (MCP `2026-07-28` `_meta`: the unprefixed `traceparent`/`tracestate`/`baggage` keys). It is carried, never interpreted, and never validated — the spec's W3C-format MUST binds the sender, and of every reserved `_meta` key it says implementations MUST NOT make assumptions about the values, so a malformed value is recorded as it arrived. ABSENT when the caller sent none — every CLI run and every legacy-era request — so a run without one is byte-identical to a run written before this field existed. WHAT IT DOES NOT GIVE YOU: token counts or cost. No run in this repo records either; `measures` states that inside the record so a reader cannot mistake a correlated run for a metered one.

measures.description: What this block accounts for. `correlation_only` means an externally-correlatable identity and NO token or cost accounting. It is a const today on purpose: the day a run records spend, this value changes and a consumer can tell the two eras of the record apart instead of inferring it from which fields happen to be present.

halt.description: A machine-readable halt SUMMARY. The full record (with call id, exit code, timestamps and the human detail) is halt-record.json — this is the pointer-free summary a reader of run-state can act on. Previously this $ref'd halt-record.schema.json, which the written artifact never satisfied (it carries only the summary fields).

reasonCode.description: the stable machine reason code (see halt-record.schema.json)
